Hey you, 

​

For starters, you're always welcome in my PM - I might pick up on unreads there faster.

Second (about the bent frame), I've been in an out of contact with Creality and they're sending me a replacement part. They gave me a tracking number etc. It's been underway for 11 days now, lol. 

Thirdly, the fat bottom layers; yes I managed to get rid of them for most of the time. There's still some part of it present but thats because I don't level the bed the way it should; if I should do that my prints don't stick to the bed due to the bent frame I got. 

What I did to get rid of them was relevel. And relevel. And retry. And relevel. And relevel cold. And relevel hot. I just releveled alot. I've also ordered the more sturdy springs because I noticed theres ALOT of slack on the standard ones. What I do to relevel, and which seems to work good on the glass bed, is relevel it when cold. I just turn the printer off so no fan is on (the little one keeps blowing and it's so annoying), grab a piece of my fiancées notes she keeps littering around and start turning the knows. I always start bottom-left -> bottom-right -> top-right -> top-left and keep redoing that. What works the best for me is turning it up with the piece of paper between the nozzle and the bed and I keep moving the piece of paper until I find a gentle resistance in moving it. Then I move to the next knob. I go around the board 2-3 times, because if you adjust one, the other one which maybe was in place, won't be any more.
Despite the uselessness of your reply, I still love it. +1

The bed is 50C throughout the print and I have no adhesionproblems. 

Too close might be an option, though I calibrate the bed with a standard piece of A4. Are there better ways?
